laws_and_bills.name: 2026-H 7331 (Kennedy) data center regulation
laws_and_bills.what: PUC must stop data centers shifting electricity costs to other customers; annual DEM reports on daily water withdrawal and cooling; DEM may require water plans; closed-loop cooling; financial assurance for site restoration. Referred to House Corporations.

laws_and_bills.name: 2026-H 7695 data center sales and use tax exemption
laws_and_bills.what: Would exempt qualified data centers and their equipment from sales and use tax (opponents say at least 30 years, no caps). House Finance hearing 2026-05-07; final outcome not found.

laws_and_bills.name: S 2427 (2026) data center grid integration / affordability
laws_and_bills.what: Would require the PUC to create a separate class of electric service for large energy use facilities such as data centers (Acadia Center testimony to Senate Commerce supports it). Final outcome not found; check whether it died at the end of the 2026 session.

local_rules.what: Town Council voted 4-1 (on or about 2026-05-05) to ban data centers; takes effect after 30 days. Hanton City Investments argues its May 4 application is grandfathered.

incentives.name: None: no data-center-specific state tax incentive found
incentives.what: Rhode Island has no data center tax incentive in NCSL's 'Status of Data Center Tax Incentives, by State (2026)' table (adapted from Husch Blackwell's 50-state survey, last updated 2026-07-27; listed as N/A; table data: https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/TQYDf/5/dataset.csv). Checked R.I. Gen. Laws 44-18-30 (sales and use tax exemptions) on 2026-10-15: no data center exemption. 2026-H 7695 would create one (see laws_and_bills). NCSL (2026-04-09) lists Rhode Island among states considering new incentives with energy and labor conditions.
